title: How a newspaper prayer turned him around in the hospital
summary: Bitter in the hospital, Cobb cut out the daily prayer from the Daily News and memorized it; it changed his life and remains his strength.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Right. All right now to get to the prayer that we talked about how I came about this prayer, is this. I'm in the hospital for the second time, and I'm bitter now.

I'm bitter with my wife, my mother, the nurses -- everybody but the doctor. And I'm getting the New York Daily News every day in the hospital; the kid brings it to me every morning -- it was 20¢ I think it was - and you see a prayer every day on the front page. Some hit you and some don't. Well, this one slapped me right in the face! I never thought of it that way. I took it and cut it out and memorized it; kept it under my pillow, and if I thought I would [destroy it], I would put it in the drawer of my desk on the side and pick it up the next morning and look at it again.

It turned me all the way around; it changed my life.
And today if I get a little despondent or depressed, I shake my head and look at it and keep going.
Yeah, I mean you had a very good reason to be sort of despondent.
Well, I can't do things like the average person can do; I'm dependent. Yet, I want to be independent, and I am independent in certain areas, and dependent in other areas, you know.
What I really meant was, you know, the pain and the boredom and everything and the three months of being in bed, and that way. I guess.
Coming on top of the first [ ] then when you got all the things set up for it of it it must have been heart-breaking. So you had to come out of it
But you have to have something to lean on to fight with, and this is my strength.
Well, you must have had a lot of guts to start with.
